long_biography.plain_text:
Born in Turin in 1962, Marco De Benedetti studied history and economics at Wesleyan University before completing an MBA at Wharton. He began in mergers and acquisitions at Wasserstein Perella, then moved through Procter & Gamble and Olivetti. At Olivetti he led telecommunications activities, chaired Infostrada and helped develop the businesses that challenged Italy's incumbent operators.

At Carlyle, De Benedetti applied that operating background to European buyouts. He advised investments including Moncler, NBTY and Golden Goose. Moncler retained him as vice-chairman and non-executive director, while CIR and Sogefi appointed him to their boards. CIR is controlled by the holding he owns with his brothers, with professional management entrusted to a chief executive.
